stem.en: A negative charge sits far from a positive one, high on the Hill. You let it go. As it falls toward the positive charge, what happens to its energy?

text.en: Its electrical potential energy turns into kinetic energy. It speeds up as it falls, like the marble.
Its potential energy stays the same.

feedback.en: On the charge-hill, "closer to the opposite charge" is downhill. Moving closer lowers its potential energy, and the difference has to go somewhere.

text.en: Its energy disappears when the two charges touch.

feedback.en: Energy is conserved. When the two charges meet, the kinetic energy of the fall becomes warmth, or light, or a spark. Nothing vanishes.

text.en: It gains energy from the positive charge.

feedback.en: Neither charge is a source. The pair together started high and ended low, and the difference came out as speed.

explanation.en: The pull between opposite charges is a slope. Falling down it converts stored energy into motion, the same as a marble. The spark you see when a charged balloon touches a doorknob is the last bit of that fall becoming light.
